headline: ARRAS HITS 935m AT 0.71% CuEq, 214.9m AT 1.42% — Berezski North Porphyry Open in All Directions; 30,000m Expansion Planned
snippet: Arras Minerals Corp. (TSX-V: ARK) reported that drill hole EL26032 at the Berezski North porphyry target in Kazakhstan returned 935.9 metres grading 0.71% CuEq from surface — the hole terminated in mineralization — including 214.9 metres at 1.42% CuEq and a high-grade breccia interval of 55 metres at 4.41% CuEq, the best result in company history. With eight holes now confirming a preserved, large porphyry system open in all directions and at depth beyond 900 metres, the high-grade breccia strike length exceeds 600 metres; results have prompted an expansion of the drill program to 30,000 metres targeting completion by end of 2026.

headline: NEEDLE MOUNTAIN OPENS STRONG — Osisko Hits 80m at 1.93% Cu (30m at 3.49%) at Gaspé; 5 Rigs Active, Zone Outside Existing MRE
snippet: Osisko Metals Inc. (TSX: OM) announced initial 2026 drill results at the Gaspé Copper Project in Quebec's Gaspé Peninsula, with hole 30-1196 in the Needle Mountain expansion area returning 80 metres grading 1.93% copper, 9.64 g/t silver, and 0.013% molybdenum from 196 metres depth, including 30 metres at 3.49% copper from 224 metres — the highest-grade intercept from this zone to date. The Needle Mountain zone sits outside the current mineral resource boundary, making these intercepts potentially additive to the project inventory; five rigs are active with two more coming on-line shortly as the 2026 infill and expansion campaign ramps.

headline: 4m AT 11.32% Cu — Marimaca Pampa Medina Returns 16m at 5.70% Cu; UHG Bornite Zone Extends, 96m Envelope at 1.19% Cu Confirmed
snippet: Marimaca Copper (TSX: MARI; ASX: MC2) reported that hole SPRD-05 at the Pampa Medina deposit in Antofagasta, Chile, intersected 96 metres at 1.19% Cu and 11.7 g/t Ag, including a 16-metre ultra-high-grade core at 5.70% Cu and 62.6 g/t Ag and 4 metres at 11.32% Cu and 144 g/t Ag — confirming a significant extension of the ultra-high-grade Bornite Zone. The sediment-hosted system continues to show strong lateral continuity across the defined 3km × 1.5km area of interest, with the 2026 program focused on high-grade zone definition, oxide extensions, and step-out testing.

headline: AMBLER METALS $35M SUMMER CAMPAIGN ACTIVE — Trilogy/South32 Deploy Drills at Arctic Cu-Zn for Mine Design Engineering
snippet: Trilogy Metals (TSX: TMQ) announced that the Ambler Metals 50/50 JV (South32 partner) has commenced its fully funded $35 million 2026 summer field program at the Upper Kobuk Mineral Projects in Alaska's Ambler Mining District, deploying 40–45 drill holes to collect geotechnical and hydrogeological data needed to advance mine design and permitting at the Arctic copper-zinc-lead-gold-silver deposit. The Arctic deposit hosts one of the world's highest-grade undeveloped copper-zinc resources; the program also re-establishes the Bornite exploration camp for a 2027 ramp-up, and marks the first fully active field season after two years of reduced activity.

headline: 27-HOLE CRITICAL MINERAL DRILL ACTIVE — Arizona G&S Tests Silverton Antimony-Gold Veins in Nevada; Open-Pit Geometry Targeted
snippet: Arizona Gold & Silver Inc. (TSX-V: AZS; OTCQB: AZASF) commenced a 27-hole reverse circulation drill program at the Silverton gold-antimony project in Nye County, Nevada, targeting high-grade antimony-bearing quartz-stibnite veins identified in historic and recent surface sampling, while testing whether the veins represent leakage from a deeper carbonate-hosted gold system. Antimony — now a U.S.-designated critical mineral — adds strategic value to the program; most holes target 30–45 metre depths amenable to open-pit extraction, with first assays expected in the coming weeks.

headline: SONORAN GOLD BELT PHASE 2 BEGINS — Questcorp + Riverside Drill 10 Holes at Historic La Union Gold-Silver District, Mexico
snippet: Questcorp Mining Inc. (CSE: QQQ) and Riverside Resources announced the commencement of a fully funded ~1,500-metre Phase 2 diamond drill campaign at the La Union Gold-Silver Project in Sonora, Mexico, testing more than five target areas across a district that historically produced an estimated 50,000 ounces of high-grade gold from oxide ores before closing in the 1950s. The program targets carbonate replacement district potential in Mexico's Sonoran Gold Belt, with Phase 1 drilling having resolved structural orientations to allow higher-confidence follow-up holes adjacent to historical mine workings.

headline: BIGGEST DRILL EVER — Standard Uranium Kicks Off 8,000m Davidson River Campaign; Athabasca Basin's Largest SW-Basin Program
snippet: Standard Uranium Ltd. (TSX-V: STND) launched its 2026 summer drill program at the Davidson River Project in southwest Athabasca Basin — the company's largest-ever campaign at 8,000 metres across two rigs targeting the Bronco, Thunderbird, and Warrior structural corridors, using Multiphysics data combined with ALS GoldSpot machine-learning to generate the company's highest-confidence targets to date. The Davidson River campaign comes in the wake of NexGen Energy's Arrow deposit and Denison Mines' Phoenix ISR receiving CNSC construction approvals in early 2026, which have drawn renewed capital attention to Saskatchewan's southwest Athabasca Basin.

headline: SEASONAL GOLD BOTTOM NEAR — Adam Hamilton: 'Least Overbought in 3 Years,' Mid-July Autumn Rally Window Opens on Schedule
snippet: Adam Hamilton's annual 'Gold Summer Doldrums' analysis, republished by GoldSeek, finds that gold has fallen to its least-overbought levels since late 2023 going into the 2026 summer seasonal trough — a setup that historically reduces the odds of a significant additional selloff in June and positions the metal for a strong autumn rally beginning around mid-July. Hamilton notes that gold-futures speculators and American stock investors both retain large re-entry capacity, and identifies 'looming war inflation' and a potential AI stock bubble correction as demand catalysts that could make 2026's autumn recovery phase unusually sharp.

headline: PHYSICAL BUYERS STEP IN — Silver Tests 200-Day Support as Retail Bargain Hunters Absorb Rate-Shock Selloff
snippet: With silver down nearly 9% following May's payrolls shock, retail physical buyers stepped in significantly at the 200-day moving average support level as bargain hunters absorbed the rate-driven selloff in one of the most pronounced physical demand surges since early 2025 — consistent with the pattern preceding prior silver recovery legs. The structural 2026 silver supply deficit of 46.3 million ounces remains intact beneath the technical weakness, providing a fundamental floor; Money Metals notes the gold-silver ratio's sharp move also adds incentive for silver repositioning at current levels.
